newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end firmer, buoyed by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares end firmer, buoyed by strong dollar.

text.p: German shares ended Tuesday's bourse trade firmer, buoyed by a firm dollar and a strong Wall Street finish on Monday.

The 30-share DAX index ended up 20.13 points, or 0.63 percent, at 3,383.19. But the IBIS DAX index, which reflects all-day electronic trade eased slightly in after-bourse trade to stand just 5.26 points higher at 3,378.22.
"Despite the relatively friendly influence from Wall Street, the German market is rather sluggish," SuedwestLB said in its morning market commentary.
Traders had looked for the DAX index to remain within a range from 3,360 to 3,400 points for the session and also possibly on Wednesday ahead of Thursday's market holiday.

But some said the DAX could break the psychologically important 3,400 level during the week and keep up the advance led by dollar-sensitive shares, particularly carmakers, if volumes were to return to the market.
"A lot will depend on when institutional investors return to the market and we can shake off this lethargic feeling," said one trader, noting the lack of fresh market orders.
Among specific shares, ball-bearings maker Kugelfischer AG reversed a strong start to end 1.10 marks lower at 29.50 marks. Earlier the company reported higher 1996 profits.
Industrial group Daimler-Benz AG which made the public introduction today in Frankfurt of its new A-class compact vehicle, was up 70 pfennigs at 127.45 marks.
Chemicals group Degussa AG was down 1.40 marks at 77.70 marks, despite reporting a 25 percent gain in first half profits and giving an optimistic outlook for the second half.
The share hit a new high of 81.25 marks in electronic trade, but traders said that while the earnings outlook was good the sales were at the lower end of expectations.
"Selling on good news" was also a factor, traders said.
